PUBLIC RESPONSE: Contracts (Remedies for Breach of Contract) Law

The principle of good faith (derived from continental civil-law traditions) was absent from the inherited Ottoman and British Mandate legislation that formed the initial basis of Israeli private law. It first appeared explicitly in Israeli statute in the Contracts (Remedies for Breach of Contract) Law of 1970, specifically in §6, which requires that remedies for breach “shall be exercised in good faith and in the customary manner.” All subsequent enactments that mention the concept (e.g., the Contracts (General Part) Law, 1973, §39) post-date this statute. Hence the Remedies Law is the earliest modern Israeli statute to introduce the term.
